name: Eligibility and conditions for taking input tax credit — section 16
definition: Section 16(2) opens 'Notwithstanding anything contained in this section' and then denies credit unless a set of conditions is met. In the source held locally those conditions are: possession of a tax invoice or debit note or other prescribed tax paying document; receipt of the goods or services; the tax charged having been actually paid to the Government; and the return under section 39 having been furnished. Three provisos qualify them: credit on the last lot where goods arrive in instalments; an add-back where the recipient does not pay the supplier within one hundred and eighty days; and re-availment once he pays.
why_it_exists: Section 16(1) states an entitlement. Section 16(2) is a separate override that converts the entitlement into a set of testable facts, so that a credit is provable from documents rather than asserted. It is the provision that makes an ITC claim auditable.
inputs: the tax invoice or debit note or other prescribed tax paying document
evidence of receipt of the goods or services
evidence that the tax charged was paid to the Government
the date of the invoice and the date the recipient paid the supplier
outputs: credit permitted, or credit denied naming the failed condition
an add-back to output tax liability where the one-hundred-and-eighty-day test fails
preconditions: the supply is not one on which credit is blocked by s.17(5)
exceptions: GST-ITC-16-2-AA — CONFLICT: a further condition appears only in the later consolidation
GST-ITC-16-2-BA — CONFLICT: a further condition appears only in the later consolidation
GST-ITC-16-5 — CONFLICT: an extended window appears only in the later consolidation
GST-ITC-16-6 — CONFLICT: revocation-of-cancellation relief appears only in the later consolidation
common_mistakes: treating the conditions as alternatives — they are cumulative; failing one denies the whole credit
taking credit on an advance payment before the goods or services are received
taking full credit on the first instalment when goods arrive in lots
ignoring the one-hundred-and-eighty-day add-back because the invoice was already booked
applying the one-hundred-and-eighty-day rule to a reverse-charge supply, which the proviso excludes
legal_references: CGST Act 2017, s.39 — the return referred to in s.16(2)(d)
CGST Act 2017, s.41 — referred to in s.16(2)(c)
icai_references: NOT APPLICABLE — a statutory eligibility test, not an accounting standard question
evidence_required: the tax invoice or debit note, held by the recipient
proof of receipt — delivery evidence, or the s.16(2)(b) Explanation route where a third party took delivery
evidence that the supplier's tax reached the Government
the payment date to the supplier, to test the one-hundred-and-eighty-day proviso
confidence_factors: weak when the document is a proforma invoice or a bare challan rather than a tax invoice or debit note
weak when receipt is inferred from the invoice date rather than evidenced
the s.16(2)(c) condition is not verifiable from the recipient's own records alone — it depends on the supplier's conduct
UNKNOWN — source is the Act as updated 31-08-2021; later amendments not held locally
CONFLICT — the second locally held source carries two further conditions, s.16(2)(aa) and s.16(2)(ba), that the primary source does not; see GST-ITC-16-2-AA and GST-ITC-16-2-BA
validation_checks: a document of a type named in s.16(2)(a) is on file
receipt is evidenced, or the deemed-receipt Explanation is satisfied
the return under s.39 for the period is filed
where goods arrived in lots, credit is taken only on receipt of the last lot
invoices unpaid beyond one hundred and eighty days are identified and added back
examples: goods delivered against a registered supplier's tax invoice, tax paid by the supplier, return filed — all four conditions met, credit permitted
counterexamples: a tax invoice held but the goods still in transit at period end — s.16(2)(b) fails, credit is not available yet
goods against one invoice received in three instalments; credit taken on the first — the first proviso denies it until the last instalment
